title: Testing the Limits
summary:
Testing the Limits
For now it seems for some owners the rosy days of 2008 when earnings reached unprecedented highs are just a fading memory. The prospects of negative timecharter equivalents (TCE) for shipowners are both overwhelming and unsustainable. While some companies have the financial fortitude to be able to bridge rough patches on retained earnings or with timecharters, others may not be so lucky.

children.title: February
children.summary: While waiting for the much anticipated seasonal uptick in gasoline demand, it now seems that it may take more than a quick activity spurt to promote a lasting recovery in the clean product tanker market. With weakening end‐user demand worldwide, it is difficult to see a rate recovery spearheaded by United States demand alone.

children.title: Tough Decisions
children.summary: As Worldscale rates continue to drop, owners trading in the spot market are rapidly approaching the razor's edge; the point at which it becomes uneconomic to move their ships. From a conventional TCE calculation perspective, based on round‐trip employment at 95% utilization, rates have been in the danger zone for weeks.

children.title: CAR‐USAC (38kt)
children.summary: HFO At current rate levels it only takes a slight increase in bunker prices to push earnings into the red. The increase in bunkers of nearly $30 per metric ton over the past two weeks has cut earnings by roughly $2,600 per day, to current levels of around $500 per day on the basis of this calculation.

children.title: Better than it Appears?
children.summary: In reality the large fleets that trade in the MR sector, whether in official pools or within large trading companies, are quite skilled at navigating through rate environments. Through consolidation of commercial control, owners can usually manage costs more effectively.
